newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma names acting privatisation head.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma names acting privatisation head.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma on Saturday named Volodymyr Lanovy as acting head of Ukraine's State Property Fund and asked parliament to approve his full appointment, the president's press service said.
"The president signed a decree naming Lanovy acting head of the fund and sent a request to parliament asking it to appoint him," the spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.
Lanovy, an economist and former deputy prime minister, will take over from Yuri Yekhanurov who was appointed minister of the economy in a cabinet reshuffle last month.
Under the constitution parliament must approve Lanovy's appointment.

Alexander Bondar, the fund's deputy chief, has said it would have to wait for a new chief before a 1997 privatisation plan could be agreed in the conservative-dominated parliament which is supervising the agency now.
Ukraine has yet to sell off any large-scale enterprises, a process which is supposed to begin this year.
Lanovy, born in 1952, was appointed state minister in charge of property and enterprise in 1991.
Later he became economy minister and set up a centre for market reforms before being appointed adviser to Kuchma on economic policy in May last year.
